title: Preview: Enforce inert body if manager is focus-trapped
body:
Closes https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/32596

Caused by https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7605

## What I did

* Added an event so that manager can inform preview it is focus trapped
* Added focus trap detection logic to manager (reads `inert` attr set by RAC on `#root` when it traps focus)
* Added focus trap event handler to preview (enforces `inert` on preview body to prevent any programmatic focus from happening)

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests:

- [ ] stories
- [ ] unit tests
- [ ] integration tests
- [ ] end-to-end tests

#### Manual testing

1. Run the code
2. Navigate to http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/overlay-modal--always-open
3. Open your favourite manager modal with the keyboard
4. Navigate within the modal with the keyboard and notice how focus isn't getting stolen any more

author: Sidnioulz

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: Technically this is the correct way do handle the callback value, but we don't really need the `forEach` nor the `if` check, since we're only observing a single element and we're using `attributeFilter`, so we know by definition that `mutations` will be a single item `{ type: 'attributes', attributeName: 'inert' }`.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: You're right, it's safe to process the event directly and it's safe to process it once.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests removing the forEach and if check since they are unnecessary given the single-element observation and attributeFilter usage.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: Please add a comment explaining why we need to track the `inert` attribute.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Explicitly requests adding a comment explaining why the inert attribute is being tracked.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body:
This should use the constant, not a magic string.

Also, the name and value of this constant does not reflect the actual event. I think it should be something like `INERT_ATTRIBUTE_CHANGED`.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
Good catch!

I initially named it `MANAGER_FOCUS_TRAP_CHANGE` because from framework/addon authors' perspective, I want the API to reflect the meaning or purpose of the event. I want third-parties to know they must stop all programmatic focus attempts. At the end of the day, I enforce a stop in the preview by also applying inert there, so it makes sense to name the event after what it actually does. I'll rename it!

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests replacing a magic string with a constant, and also suggests renaming the constant to better reflect the actual event.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: Add a comment explaining what this is for (synchronizing `inert` between manager and preview).
